note: F5's final task, and the second of the feature's two REJECTs. The defect was worth the cycle: F4.5's 30-second soft cap ends a take with nobody pressing Stop, and _pump_loop noticed, pushed onCaptureEnded and exited WITHOUT stopping the camera — so pressing Record and walking away left the webcam lit and the preview streaming indefinitely, on a routine path, against a requirement spec.md 1.1 and 4 make a headline ('Pressing Stop reverts the disk to the smiley and RELEASES THE CAMERA'). Writing the test for that fix then exposed a second, independent ordering bug: start_record called _start_pump() BEFORE _start_camera(), so the loop that tears the camera down could run before the camera had started. Unreachable with a real 30s cap, but wrong on its own terms and fixed. Both fixes were mutation-checked 4/4 by the implementor and the primary fix independently re-mutated by the verifier. Learn scan outcome: a lesson cleared the bar and is PROPOSED, pending human approval; project.md was NOT written unapproved. Its evidence is unusually strong because the SAME code path has now caused a defect in TWO consecutive features: F4.5 existed because the 30-second cap path deadlocked the PortAudio callback, and F5 Task 7 was rejected because that same cap path failed to release the camera. A path that ends an operation without user action is exactly where teardown gets forgotten, because every test and every manual check naturally drives the explicit Stop. Overlap-checked across problem, root cause, fix, files and prevention against the four existing guardrails and the two already-parked proposals: distinct from all of them — the earned 'no unexercised branch' rule and parked proposal A ('a test must assert something that would break if the behaviour were removed') both concern test quality, whereas this concerns enumerating the exit paths of a resource's lifetime before writing any test at all. Enforcement was considered per learn step 5 and rejected: no lint rule can know which resources are scoped to which operation, and the honest mechanism is a review question. NOTE this makes THREE parked, unapproved guardrail proposals (A from Task 5, B from Task 3, C here) — deliberately presented to the human together at the feature-end checkpoint rather than dribbled out, and worth weighing against the fact that curate is now DUE (10 verdicts since the last curate). No ADR for this task specifically, but F5's underlying architecture decision DID clear the 3-condition gate at feature completion and was written as adr/0004-python-owns-the-camera.md.
